content.title: The SUV that quietly matches Lexus in owner satisfaction
content.text: Credit: Mazda Published Apr 7, 2026, 12:30 PM EDT Adam Gray, a seasoned automotive journalist and content creator from the UK, joined the How-To Geek editorial team in January 2025. As an automotive journalist for How-To Geek, Adam breaks first-to-report news on the latest in automotive tech, as well as penning automotive features and reviews. Adam is also a contributor to one of How-To Geek's sister sites, TopSpeed, where he uses his media accrediation with manufacturers' press offices to gain access to the latest vehicles for subsequent review. Prior to joining How-To Geek, Adam worked on a freelance basis, contributing automotive content to a variety of business and lifestyle publications. His experience also includes time spent serving as senior editorial & auction content manager for SBX Cars, automotive content writer for Supercar Blondie, motoring editor for Portfolio North, and motoring editor - North East for Reach plc. When he's not putting the latest vehicle through its paces or testing out its tech, Adam can be found at his local ice rink playing ice hockey or at the Riverside Stadium supporting his beloved Middlesbrough FC. Adam also enjoys spending quality time with his three children: Ellie, Oscar, and Heidi. Sign in to your How-To Geek account For a long time, if you wanted a hassle-free, feel-good SUV, luxury brands were the obvious choice. Reliability, comfort, and consistency made them the safe bet—until now. Mainstream SUVs are stepping up, quietly matching the refinement and dependability that once only came with a fancy badge. Smarter engineering and better materials are leveling the playing field. Today’s buyers know what matters: low maintenance, durability, and everyday usability. That’s why some unexpected SUVs are now giving the luxury crowd a run for their money. In order to give you the most up-to-date and accurate information possible, the data used to compile this article was sourced from Mazda and other authoritative sources, including CarEdge, iSeeCars, J.D. Power, RepairPal, and TopSpeed. Related This Toyota hybrid makes some luxury SUVs hard to justify Turns out you don’t need a luxury badge to feel spoiled—this Toyota SUV is refined and seriously comfortable. SUV buyers are discovering that premium satisfaction doesn’t require a luxury badge How mainstream models are matching comfort, reliability, and quality once reserved for luxury brands Credit: Lexus But things are changing. Mainstream SUVs are stepping up, and the Mazda CX-5 is quietly showing it can hang with the luxury crowd—without the hefty price tag or high maintenance. Owner satisfaction isn’t just about first impressions anymore. Metrics like “would I buy it again?” and how well a car holds up over time show the CX-5 consistently punching above its weight. Related Why This Used Mazda Crossover Won Me Over Instantly Agile handling, upscale touches, and everyday practicality make this used crossover an instant standout. What makes the CX-5 feel like a luxury SUV without costing a luxury price The design, engineering, and reliability tweaks that give mainstream buyers a premium experience Under the hood, buyers get a choice of two familiar engines. The standard 2.5-liter four-cylinder pumps out 187 horsepower and 186 lb-ft of torque, while the turbo version cranks up to 256 horsepower and 320 lb-ft on premium fuel. Both stick with a six-speed automatic, even as many rivals have switched to CVTs. That traditional setup isn’t just old-school—it actually shapes the CX-5’s character. The six-speed automatic shifts smoothly and predictably, making driving feel natural and engaging, and it tends to last longer, which is a big part of why owners stay happy for the long haul. Every detail inside the CX-5 is built to feel premium Inside, the cabin feels more premium than its price suggests. Soft-touch surfaces, available leather, and a clean, driver-focused layout make it stand out from other compact SUVs. Noise insulation is another highlight. Road and wind noise are minimal, while supportive seats and intuitive controls create a quiet, refined driving experience. Related The Most Reliable New SUV You Can Buy for Under $45,000 This dependable SUV combines durability, comfort, and smart tech, making it a top pick under $45K for buyers who value long-term peace of mind. Why CX-5 owners hang on to their SUVs longer than most The design, comfort, and reliability choices that make it hard to let go Credit: Mazda One of the clearest signs a car is doing something right is how long people keep it. CX-5 owners often hang on longer than expected, and it’s easy to see why. The naturally aspirated engine is especially durable and easy to maintain. Keeping things simple means fewer headaches, lower repair costs, and more confidence for owners over the long haul. Reliability scores just confirm what owners already know Credit: Mazda The CX-5 shines in reliability ratings across the board. J.D. Power ranks it in the “great” category, while iSeeCars gives it a 7.9 out of 10, predicting an average lifespan of 14 years or 164k miles. There’s even a 22 percent chance a CX-5 will reach 200k miles, giving owners extra peace of mind. Average annual maintenance: $447 (RepairPal) Estimated cost over 10 years: $7,906 (CarEdge) Total recalls: None (NHTSA) The CX-5 is fun to drive, and owners love it for that Credit: Mazda Reliability isn’t the only reason CX-5 owners hang on for the long haul. The driving experience matters just as much. Unlike many compact SUVs that sacrifice fun for practicality, the CX-5 feels engaging and connected. The steering is precise, the chassis is balanced, and it drives more like a sporty sedan than a typical crossover. That mix of dependability and driving enjoyment builds a real attachment. When a car continues to meet needs and makes daily drives rewarding, owners aren’t in a rush to trade it in. Related Best Budget-Friendly Used SUV to Buy in 2025 Reliable, practical, and packed with value, this used SUV stands out in 2025 as the smartest budget-friendly buy for savvy shoppers. Why this mainstream SUV feels premium without the luxury price tag Credit: Mazda Comparing a mainstream SUV to Lexus might sound ambitious, but the CX-5 holds its own. Across key ownership metrics, it proves surprisingly competitive. Reliability is where Lexus usually sets the bar, but the CX-5 comes close. Its proven components and consistent performance mean fewer issues and strong long-term satisfaction. Comfort is another area where it shines. The cabin is quiet, the seats are supportive, and the ride hits a sweet spot between soft and controlled. The interior quality impresses, too. While it doesn’t match high-end luxury, the materials and design feel upscale, giving a premium vibe without the luxury price tag. Credit: Mazda Daily usability is where the CX-5 really shines. Luxury SUVs can overwhelm with flashy touchscreens and menus that look good but aren’t always easy to use. The CX-5 keeps things simple. Its infotainment is controlled with a rotary dial, and physical buttons for key functions stay front and center, so you don’t have to dig through menus while driving. This practical approach makes everyday driving easier and adds to a long-term ownership experience that’s both comfortable and stress-free. Cost of ownership gives the CX-5 another edge. With a lower sticker price and reasonable maintenance and repair costs, it’s easy on the wallet without cutting corners. For many buyers, that balance matters more than the prestige of a luxury badge. The CX-5 proves you don’t need to spend extra to get reliability, comfort, and daily usability. Related The Perfect Used Three-Row SUV for Driving Enthusiasts With Families This used three-row SUV blends driving excitement with family comfort, offering luxury, agility, and great value in one package. Why the CX-5 delivers comfort, reliability, and usability that rivals pricier rivals Credit: Mazda What really sets the CX-5 apart is how it delivers a near-luxury experience without the usual trade-offs. Luxury SUVs can impress with comfort and tech, but they come with higher costs and potentially pricey maintenance. Mainstream SUVs are easier on the wallet but often lack refinement and engaging driving dynamics. The CX-5 bridges that gap effortlessly. Inside, the cabin feels premium thanks to quality materials and thoughtful design, while the price stays accessible. On the road, it’s engaging to drive without sacrificing comfort or practicality. Mazda’s focus on proven engineering over flashy, untested tech makes a big difference. Reliability and consistency mean fewer headaches and a smoother long-term ownership experience. Credit: Mazda Standard all-wheel drive adds extra confidence behind the wheel, helping the CX-5 handle a variety of road conditions with ease. Pair that with a full suite of safety features, and you’ve got a well-rounded SUV that fits modern drivers’ needs. The CX-5’s strength is its balance. It doesn’t try to beat luxury brands at every turn, but it also doesn’t settle for “just okay.” That careful blend of reliability, comfort, and usability is why owners keep their CX-5s for years. Lexus may still set the bar, but the CX-5 proves you can hit similar long-term satisfaction without the luxury price tag.
